OWASP_Top_10.name: OWASP Top 10 2021
OWASP_Top_10.intro: The OWASP Top 10 is the most widely referenced standard for web application security risks, published by the Open Web Application Security Project. It identifies the ten most critical vulnerability categories affecting web applications globally. Compliance with the relevant OWASP Top 10 categories is a baseline expectation for any application handling user data or financial transactions.

requirements.name: Broken Access Control
requirements.description: Restrictions on what authenticated users are allowed to do are not properly enforced. Includes clickjacking, CORS misconfigurations, and frame-based attacks.
requirements.fix: Set X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN or use CSP frame-ancestors directive. Remove CORS wildcard (*) and allowlist only trusted origins.

requirements.name: Cryptographic Failures
requirements.description: Failures related to cryptography which expose sensitive data in transit. Includes missing HTTPS enforcement, weak TLS, and insecure cookies.
requirements.fix: Enforce HTTPS with Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS). Set the Secure flag on all cookies. Eliminate mixed HTTP/HTTPS content.

requirements.name: Injection (XSS)
requirements.description: Cross-site scripting (XSS) allows attackers to inject client-side scripts into web pages viewed by other users. A strong Content Security Policy is the primary browser-side defence.
requirements.fix: Deploy a Content Security Policy. Avoid 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' — use nonces or hashes for inline scripts instead.

requirements.name: Security Misconfiguration
requirements.description: Insecure default configurations, incomplete configurations, or misconfigured HTTP headers that expose unnecessary attack surface.
requirements.fix: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy. Remove server version headers (Server, X-Powered-By).

requirements.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
requirements.description: Components (libraries, frameworks) running with known vulnerabilities. Subresource Integrity (SRI) ensures external scripts have not been tampered with.
requirements.fix: Add integrity= and crossorigin= attributes to all external <script> and <link> tags. Use npm audit / pip audit to find vulnerable packages.

requirements.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
requirements.description: Authentication weaknesses including session cookie misconfigurations that allow session hijacking.
requirements.fix: Set HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax (or Strict) on all session cookies to prevent JavaScript access and CSRF-based session theft.

requirements.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
requirements.description: Code and infrastructure that does not protect against integrity violations. Includes CI/CD pipeline integrity and client-side supply chain attacks via unverified scripts.
requirements.fix: Deploy SRI for all externally loaded scripts and stylesheets. Use a strict CSP to prevent loading from untrusted origins.

PCI_DSS.name: PCI-DSS v4.0
PCI_DSS.intro: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) is a mandatory security standard for organisations that handle credit card payments. Version 4.0, effective from March 2024, strengthens requirements around web application security. Any web application that processes, stores, or transmits cardholder data must meet these technical controls at the application layer.

requirements.name: Strong Cryptography in Transit
requirements.description: All cardholder data transmitted over open, public networks must be encrypted with strong cryptography and use accepted security protocols only.
requirements.fix: Use TLS 1.2 or 1.3. Deploy HSTS to prevent protocol downgrade. Remove all mixed HTTP resources from HTTPS pages.

requirements.name: Public-Facing Web Application Protection
requirements.description: Public-facing web applications must be protected against known attacks via security controls — including injection attacks, broken access control, and cross-site scripting.
requirements.fix: Deploy a Content Security Policy. Set X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options headers. Conduct regular vulnerability assessments.

requirements.name: Payment Page Script Management
requirements.description: All scripts loaded on payment pages must be authorised, have their integrity verified, and be inventoried to prevent supply-chain skimming attacks.
requirements.fix: Add Subresource Integrity (integrity= attribute) to all external scripts. Use a strict CSP allowlist to restrict script sources.

requirements.name: Secure Transmission of Authentication Credentials
requirements.description: Authentication credentials must not be transmitted in cleartext or in a way that can be intercepted by attackers on the network.
requirements.fix: Ensure all authentication endpoints use HTTPS. Set Secure flag on all authentication cookies. Enable HSTS to prevent downgrade.

requirements.name: Cryptographic Algorithm Review
requirements.description: All in-use cryptographic algorithms, keys, and certificates must be documented and reviewed at least once every 12 months to ensure they remain strong.
requirements.fix: Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Disable weak cipher suites (RC4, 3DES, export ciphers). Renew certificates before expiry.

GDPR_Article_32.name: GDPR Article 32
GDPR_Article_32.intro: Article 32 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires controllers and processors to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including encryption of personal data and ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of processing systems. These obligations apply to any organisation processing EU/EEA personal data.

requirements.name: Encryption of Personal Data in Transit
requirements.description: Pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data. Web applications must encrypt all data in transit between the browser and server.
requirements.fix: Enforce HTTPS on all endpoints. Deploy HSTS. Set the Secure flag on all cookies containing session identifiers or personal data.

requirements.name: Ongoing Confidentiality and Integrity
requirements.description: The ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of processing systems and services must be ensured.
requirements.fix: Deploy CSP to prevent content injection. Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Remove server version disclosure headers.

requirements.name: Resilience and Availability
requirements.description: Ability to restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident.
requirements.fix: Publish CAA records to restrict certificate authorities. Configure SPF and DMARC to prevent email spoofing that could enable phishing attacks targeting your users.

requirements.name: Regular Testing and Assessment
requirements.description: A process for regularly testing, assessing, and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures for ensuring security of processing.
requirements.fix: Enforce DMARC policy (p=quarantine or p=reject). Set Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy to limit data leakage. Conduct periodic security assessments.

ISO_27001.name: ISO 27001:2022 Annex A
ISO_27001.intro: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 is the international standard for information security management systems (ISMS). Annex A provides a reference set of controls that organisations must consider for their ISMS. The 2022 revision introduced four new technology-specific controls relevant to web application security. Certification requires documented implementation of applicable controls and ongoing monitoring.

requirements.name: Web Filtering
requirements.description: Access to external websites must be managed to reduce exposure to malicious content. On the server side, CSP restricts what external resources your web application loads.
requirements.fix: Implement a Content Security Policy with a strict allowlist for script, style, and resource sources. Remove CORS wildcards.

requirements.name: Use of Cryptography
requirements.description: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, must be defined and implemented.
requirements.fix: Use TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites. Enforce HSTS. Protect session cookies with the Secure flag.

requirements.name: Secure Development Life Cycle
requirements.description: Rules for the secure development of software and systems must be established and applied. Includes supply-chain integrity controls.
requirements.fix: Add Subresource Integrity to all external scripts and stylesheets. Eliminate HTTP resources loaded on HTTPS pages.

requirements.name: Application Security Requirements
requirements.description: Information security requirements must be identified, specified, and approved when developing or acquiring applications.
requirements.fix: Deploy the full set of recommended security headers: CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy.

requirements.name: Monitoring Activities
requirements.description: Networks, systems, and applications must be monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken to evaluate potential information security incidents.
requirements.fix: Configure SPF and DMARC with p=quarantine or p=reject to receive delivery reports and detect email spoofing of your domain.

requirements.name: Information Transfer
requirements.description: Information transfer rules, procedures, and controls must be in place for all types of transfer facilities within the organisation and with external parties.
requirements.fix: Enforce HSTS. Eliminate mixed content. Set SameSite=Lax or Strict on cookies to prevent cross-site data transfer.
